title: Canonical RHom evaluation on a strictly perfect neighbourhood
statement: Let X be a scheme [def-pc-scheme] and K,N objects of D(O_X) [def-pc-derived-category], with derived categories also on every open. Let U be an open and P a strictly perfect complex over U [def-pc-perfect-complex], with K|U isomorphic to QP. Put D=RHom(K,O_X) [def-pur-derived-internal-hom]. For the canonical tensor-internal-Hom family e of [def-pc-canonical-derived-tensor-hom-bijection], put ev=e(D,K,O_X)(id_D). The restriction to U of e(N tensor D,K,N)^(-1)(alpha; id_N tensor ev; rho) is an isomorphism. Tensor, alpha and rho are the shared derived tensor structure [def-pc-scheme-derived-tensor-structure]. No perfectness is required away from U, and N need not be bounded or quasi-coherent.

source.place: Tag 08DQ, proof of Lemma 20.50.5 after reducing to a strictly perfect representative; Tag 08DM, Lemma 20.46.9

proof.text: Use exact restriction to U on complexes. Restriction of sheaf tensor, sums, and Hom is computed over the same opens V contained in U. Thus the K-flat tensor model and K-injective internal-Hom model restrict to the corresponding models over U. For Hom this is the restriction isomorphism of 08DL, obtained by restricting the components of the Hom complex. The defining representative equation of the canonical tensor-Hom family identifies the restricted evaluation adjunct with the local ordinary tensor-Hom comparison. Transport the first variable along the given derived isomorphism K|U ≅ QP. This is a comparison of maps, not merely an identification of source and target objects.

Write E=P. The proof of 08DM computes RHom(E,O_U) by the ordinary Hom complex; its degree q term is Hom(E^(-q),O_U). Each E^i is a retract of O_U^m. Dualizing its retraction shows that Hom(E^i,O_U) is a retract of O_U^m, hence flat. Since E has only finitely many nonzero degrees, the dual is bounded and is K-flat by the bounded-above flat site lemma. Thus tensoring this dual with any representative F of N|U computes the derived tensor. No boundedness or quasi-coherence is imposed on F. The existing strictly-perfect Hom wrapper assumes U affine: on a non-affine U use the same source argument locally on affine subopens and check the quasi-isomorphism on cohomology sheaves, rather than applying that wrapper without its affine hypothesis.

Apply the same Hom computation to RHom(E,F). In degree n the comparison is the sum, over p+q=n, of F^p tensor Hom(E^(-q),O_U) → Hom(E^(-q),F^p). The bounded support of E makes the sum finite. For E^(-q)=O_U^m, evaluating on the m basis sections identifies both sides with (F^p)^m and the comparison with the identity. The formula is natural contravariantly in E^(-q), so a retract of O_U^m gives a retract of this isomorphism; the inverse restricts to the retract too. Therefore every degree map is invertible.

The componentwise comparison is a chain map: composing evaluation with the F differential gives the first term of the total differential, and composing with the E-dual differential gives the second term with its Koszul sign. This is also the uncurrying equation of the canonical tensor-Hom family. A degreewise invertible chain map is an isomorphism of complexes, so its image in the derived category is invertible. Step 1 identifies it with the restricted map in the statement. For empty U or zero E all terms are zero and the same argument applies.
